# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy.

Hypothesis and context. In neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy, a setting relevant to sporadic ALS with TDP-43 pathology, phosphorylation of an FG-nucleoporin is proposed as a pore-intrinsic intermediate required to sustain nuclear-import failure. Nup98 is only the pre-registered lead. The single-gene claim stays provisional until NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics ranks it first. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 de-mixing is the initiating event. Nucleoporin phosphorylation is proposed to maintain import suppression. Nuclear TDP-43 depletion, broader transport failure, and neuronal death are downstream responses. The claim is limited to this TDP-43 context.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components; disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in cell systems, and related pore pathology is present in ALS tissue [S1]. These data support a TDP-43–pore connection and leave the initiating modification unidentified. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to RanGAP mislocalization and impaired nuclear import, and transport-related manipulations modify phenotypes in that genetic context [S2]. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form without conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death; phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in the assemblies [S3]. That TDP-43 modification is separate from nucleoporin phosphorylation. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies those defects [S4]. Together, [S3] and [S4] separate stress-granule sequestration from a stress-granule-independent TDP-43 route. No supplied source shows that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS.

Speculative bridges. Nup98 identity, phosphosites, and the kinase remain assumptions until the gate below is passed. Unverified prior knowledge outside this packet is that FG-nucleoporins can be phosphorylated during mitosis or stress in non-ALS cells; that background leaves the same events in ALS unestablished. The assumed bridge is that cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies direct a kinase to the ranked FG-nucleoporin and that the modification sustains import blockade. No packet source demonstrates that interaction.

Discovery gate and favored step. NPC-fraction phosphoproteomics is ordered against cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies. A site cluster is included only if three pre-registered rules all hold: the phosphopeptide maps to an NPC-resident FG-nucleoporin in the NPC fraction; occupancy exceeds a pre-set fold-change and stoichiometry threshold versus matched baseline; and the rise precedes nuclear TDP-43 loss and death markers. Rank equals occupancy change weighted by temporal precedence. Nup98 enters allele tests only at rank 1; otherwise the top-ranked FG-nucleoporin replaces it. The kinase assigned by those data is then tested by inhibition or a kinase-dead allele that lowers included-site phosphorylation while imaged assemblies remain intact. The single favored step is altered FG-repeat selective permeability, read as the initial NLS-cargo import rate in permeabilized neurons supplied with excess Ran and transport factors. Quantitative NPC-composition mass spectrometry is the retirement assay: restored import rate with disease-matched subunit stoichiometry retires a composition mechanism; normalized stoichiometry without import rescue retires the FG-permeability step.

Alternatives. Transport factors may be sequestered in stress granules, so import fails without a covalent pore change [S4]. TDP-43 aggregates may mislocalize nucleoporins directly, leaving phosphorylation as a bystander [S1]. In C9orf72 models, RanGAP mislocalization may explain import failure without FG-nucleoporin phosphorylation [S2]. Import failure may also follow nonspecific cellular stress.

Discriminating preclinical test. Four arms use iPSC-derived motor neurons. Arm 1 locks induction to a cytoplasm-enriched TDP-43 de-mixing construct that forms persistent assemblies while G3BP1 stays dispersed, matching the stress-granule-independent route [S3]; constructs that nucleate conventional stress granules are excluded. Arm 2 uses the same TDP-43 perturbation with stress granules intact. Arm 3 applies one pre-registered intervention that prevents G3BP1-positive granules, without TDP-43 de-mixing, and must keep NLS-reporter import inside a pre-registered null window of unstressed baseline; a method that itself impairs import is invalid. Arm 4 is a C9orf72 repeat-RNA model without engineered TDP-43 assemblies [S2]. Included sites only are swapped at near-endogenous dosage for phospho-null or phospho-mimetic alleles, with total TDP-43 held constant. Readouts are NLS-reporter import, permeabilized initial import rate, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, NPC composition, nucleoporin and RanGAP localization, stress-granule markers, and delayed death. Predictions in arm 1: included phosphorylation follows assemblies and precedes death; phospho-null and on-target kinase blockade each preserve permeabilized import rate and nuclear TDP-43 despite intact assemblies. Context-specificity fails if the phospho-null gain in NLS import rate in arm 4 exceeds 0.25 times the gain in arm 1.

Falsifying observation. Absence of any site meeting the three inclusion rules while import is already impaired falsifies the hypothesis before allele construction. Confirmed absence of the mapped modification on phospho-null protein, with unchanged kinetics and severity of import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and death in arm 1, also falsifies it. Phosphorylation only after death markers marks a late correlate. Joint disappearance of the transport defect and of phosphorylation when stress granules are suppressed favors sequestration [S4]. No import phenotype for both phospho-null and phospho-mimetic alleles falsifies a functional role for the included sites. Kinase blockade that leaves import impaired while assemblies remain intact falsifies phosphorylation as the required intermediate. An arm-4 effect above the 0.25 bound retires the context-specific claim.

Limitations. Site and kinase identity must be measured. Redundant phosphorylation of other nucleoporins can yield a false-negative single-gene result. Phospho-mimetic substitutions omit kinase timing and localization. Cultured neurons compress a years-long human disease, and TDP-43-model results stay tied to the tested context rather than transferring automatically to C9orf72 or SOD1 ALS. The design tests necessity and order in preclinical systems and stops short of therapy validation.

Ranked proposal:
Provisional Nup98 phosphorylation after stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assembly sustains nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy
